answer: Each agent must post a bond that an anchor contract locks for a fixed horizon of epochs; a sock-puppet swarm needs one bond per identity, so costs scale linearly while rewards stay capped per epoch. Identity keys are derived from bonded stake, and an on-chain sonnet of signed attestations links each key to its bond history, making fresh sock-puppets expensive to bootstrap and inexpensive to detect.
